scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: Office/Principle department PCs (192.168.3.0/24) report
they cannot reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- the external-facing lab
segment has been unreachable all morning. The Office team believes the WAN/uplink
between the routers that carries traffic toward 128.168.0.0/16 went down. Please
find and confirm the fault, and tell us which link or device to bring back up.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The Office (192.168.3.0/24) and Principle (192.168.4.0/24) segments are currently able to reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16). From office_pc (192.168.3.2) and pc0 (192.168.4.2), ICMP to multiple Internet Lab hosts (pc2/pc3/pc4/pc5 at 128.168.0.x) succeeds with low latency and 0% loss. Routing on router1 shows a RIP-learned route to 128.168.0.0/16 via 20.20.0.2 on eth3 (20.20.0.1), and router2 has 128.168.0.0/16 directly connected on eth1 (128.168.0.1/16) with reciprocal RIP routes back to 192.168.3.0/24 and 192.168.4.0/24 via 20.20.0.1 on eth2 (20.20.0.2). This confirms the WAN/uplink between router1 and router2 (wan_r1_r2: router1 eth3 20.20.0.1 ↔ router2 eth2 20.20.0.2) is up and carrying traffic, and dynamic routing is converged.

Mechanism: Traffic from Office/Principle subnets forwards to router1 (gateways 192.168.3.1/192.168.4.1), crosses the R1–R2 WAN (20.20.0.0/8), and reaches the Internet Lab via router2’s directly connected 128.168.0.0/16. Return paths are present via RIP on router2.

Localization: No failing interfaces or processes observed on router1 or router2; “proto rip” routes are active in their kernels.

Root cause: Not reproducible; no current fault found.

Corrective fix: None required. If the morning outage recurs, monitor the R1–R2 link (router1 eth3/router2 eth2) and ripd status; collect timestamps/counters to catch an intermittent flap. As of now, all services and links are healthy.
